description:
FILED s451z, MEASURED, with the reason the obvious fix is wrong.

    # t/op/filetest.t:112
    use Perl::OSType 'os_type';
    if (os_type ne 'Unix') { ... }

        perl  calls os_type()
        PCL   emits the STRING "os_type"  ->  (p-str-ne "os_type" "Unix")

`Pl::Parser::_parse_use_import_list` reads a `qw()` list and a parenthesised
list, but PPI hands an UNPARENTHESISED single quote over as a DIRECT CHILD of
the Include statement, so the list came back EMPTY -- which every caller reads
as "no import list at all".

WHY THE ONE-LINE FIX IS WRONG (measured s451z, emission A/B over 1036 files):
adding the bare-quote arm unconditionally moved three
cpan-tests/Test-Simple-1.302199/t/Legacy/Builder files, because
`use Test::More 'no_plan'` is syntactically identical and 'no_plan' is an
ARGUMENT, not an import name.  A non-empty import list makes
`_merge_module_prototypes` restrict the merge to those names, so Test::More's
`is($$;$)` never arrived and every `is(...)` argument lost scalar context.

So the arm exists but is OPT-IN (`bare_quote => 1`), used today only by
#703's `use subs` pre-pass, where every argument IS a name.

FIX SHAPE (not designed): the reading has to come from the MODULE, not from
the syntax -- e.g. only treat a bare quote as an import name when the module's
own @EXPORT/@EXPORT_OK scan (the one `_extract_module_prototypes` already
runs) contains it.  That is data PCL already has for the modules it can read.

BAR: filetest.t's `os_type` row; the three Test-Simple files byte-identical;
`use POSIX ':sys_wait_h'` (a TAG, not a name) unchanged; emission A/B over the
four populations.
subject: `use Module 'name'` (unparenthesised, single name) is not read as an import list, so an imported prototype-less sub stays a bareword STRING -- and the naive fix breaks Test::More
